Implemented and merged:

- [PR #2438](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2438) removed all 43 Blacksmith runner labels and five vendor Docker actions. Repository-wide Blacksmith references are now zero.
- [PR #2442](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/pull/2442) parallelized integration tests and package builds.
- Squash commit: `ad2d42a4e`.
- Full [`main` CI](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/actions/runs/30778305132) passed.
- Worktree and task branch cleaned up.
- No Opus review was used; Fable was attempted but quota-exhausted.

Performance:

- Before optimization, Blacksmith was about **2.6× faster**: 4m29s versus 11m52s on GitHub-hosted runners.
- Historical medians were similar: 4.45m on Blacksmith versus 12.2m before Blacksmith, approximately **2.7× faster / 64% less time**.
- After this change, GitHub-hosted integration compute dropped from **7m54s to 4m09s**, approximately **47% faster**. The individual workers now finish in 2m43s–3m21s.
- Package builds dropped locally from 68.7s to 40.8s, approximately **41% faster**.

Where the remaining time goes:

- Under normal capacity, the required CI path is now around four minutes.
- Under heavy organization-wide concurrency, queueing dominates. The final `main` run took 25m19s because integration workers were admitted over a 12-minute span, and the four-second aggregate waited another 9m19s for a runner.
- The next safe improvement is migrating branch protection to require the four real integration jobs directly, then deleting the aggregate job. I did not change required contexts immediately because that would strand currently open PRs.

Runner recommendation: **stay with standard GitHub-hosted runners for now**. They are free for this public repository, whereas larger runners are always billed and self-hosting still costs infrastructure and maintenance. GitHub also warns that self-hosted runners should almost never execute public-repository PRs because untrusted code can persistently compromise them. [GitHub Actions billing](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions), [runner security guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use).

If queueing remains frequent after the required-check migration, the viable paid path is isolated, ephemeral ARC runners on dedicated non-production infrastructure—not a persistent runner inside the production cluster. [ARC guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/use-actions-runner-controller/quickstart).

One external item remains: the Blacksmith GitHub App still has “all repositories” access with Actions/workflow write permissions. GitHub’s API cannot safely convert that installation to selected repositories, and no paired browser was available. It should be scoped manually at [the Lobu organization installation settings](https://github.com/organizations/lobu-ai/settings/installations/136316292), excluding `lobu` and `owletto`; I deliberately did not uninstall it from the other 11 repositories.

so did we make the ci still faster? we target for less than 5 mins

Not reliably. We made the CI execution faster, but we have not consistently achieved the under-five-minute wall-clock target.

- Test execution: **7m54s → approximately 4m09s**, about **47% faster**.
- Best post-change run: required integration passed in **4m47s**, meeting the target.
- Other runs took **7m32s**, **23m59s**, and **25m19s** because GitHub queued the parallel jobs and then queued the three-second aggregate check.

So the code is fast enough; runner availability is now the bottleneck.

To reliably stay below five minutes, we need:

1. Migrate branch protection to require the four integration workers directly, then remove the aggregate job. This removes its 3–9 minute queue tail.
2. Ensure four runners can start together. A single cheap self-hosted runner would serialize them and miss the target.
3. Either reduce organization-wide CI fan-out or provide dedicated ephemeral capacity. Standard hosted runners remain cheapest, but they cannot guarantee the target during bursts.

Verdict: **faster, yes; dependable sub-five-minute CI, not yet.**

Verdict: don’t use the personal Mac mini for public-PR CI. It won’t accelerate Lobu’s required Linux path, and GitHub explicitly warns that public-repo self-hosted runners can be persistently compromised.

Key findings:

- Lobu is public on GitHub Free. Standard hosted runners are free and unlimited for public repositories; Free allows 20 concurrent jobs.
- Required compute checks all run on Ubuntu. Integration uses Postgres service containers, which self-hosted runners support only on Linux with Docker.
- The Mac smoke is optional, not branch-required.
- No repository self-hosted runner is registered, and no local Actions runner process/service was detected. Org-wide runners couldn’t be enumerated due missing `admin:org`.
- The current `ci-subfive` required-first topology is the best zero-cost fix. `ubuntu-slim` remains in the same concurrency pool, so it is useful for tiny aggregators but doesn’t add capacity.

Only trusted post-merge work is a reasonable Mac candidate:

- `mac-release`
- The Darwin ARM64 pgvector artifact build
- A separately split, main-only Mac smoke

Keep PR Mac smoke GitHub-hosted. If the Mac is eventually used, isolate it from personal credentials and LAN access, use a dedicated label/group, and preferably wipe or recreate its environment between jobs.

Next scaling lever after measuring the new CI topology: request a hosted concurrency increase from GitHub Support. GitHub documents that this limit can be increased.

Official sources: [hosted runner pricing/specifications](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners), [20-job Free concurrency limit](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits), [public self-hosted runner warning](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use#hardening-for-self-hosted-runners), [self-hosted requirements](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/self-hosted-runners).
